+"""Record preparation steps."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from click.utils import make_default_short_help
+
+DISPLAY_MAX_LENGTH = 20
+
+
+def summarize(value: str, max_length: int = DISPLAY_MAX_LENGTH) -> str:
+    """Condense help text with the click default short-help semantics."""
+    return make_default_short_help(value, max_length)
+
+
+def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    """Validate ``record`` and return a new prepared dict.
+
+    The result has exactly ``key`` (trimmed), ``value`` (unchanged),
+    ``display`` (condensed ``value``) and ``enabled``. The input is never
+    mutated. Invalid records raise :class:`ValueError`.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(record, dict):
+        raise ValueError("record must be a dict")
+
+    key = record.get("key")
+
+    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
+        raise ValueError("record key must be a nonempty string")
+
+    if "value" not in record:
+        raise ValueError("record must have a value")
+
+    value = record["value"]
+
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        raise ValueError("record value must be a string")
+
+    enabled = record.get("enabled", True)
+
+    if not isinstance(enabled, bool):
+        raise ValueError("record enabled must be a bool")
+
+    return {
+        "key": key.strip(),
+        "value": value,
+        "display": summarize(value),
+        "enabled": enabled,
+    }

--- a/src/reusebench_click_summary/steps.py
+++ b/src/reusebench_click_summary/steps.py
@@ -48,3 +48,25 @@ def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
         "display": summarize(value),
         "enabled": enabled,
     }
+
+
+def batch(records: t.Any) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]:
+    """Prepare each record in order, rejecting duplicate trimmed keys."""
+    if not isinstance(records, list):
+        raise ValueError("records must be a list")
+
+    prepared = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+
+    for record in records:
+        item = prepare(record)
+
+        key = item["key"]
+
+        if key in seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate record key: {key!r}")
+
+        seen.add(key)
+        prepared.append(item)
+
+    return prepared

+def merge(left: t.Any, right: t.Any) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]:
